The list loads again each time its tab shows again. A row opens its page in a new tab (⌘-click or middle-click: behind); its × or its menu (Open in New Tab, Open in Background, Copy Link, Remove from History) removes every visit to the page. The page asks main only about its own tab's profile and opens only pages it listed (D53). The Library keeps its History section, the same list. Clearing the Archive leaves history alone

AR-11.note: Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that; a deleted profile’s Favorites, Spaces and tabs are taken out of every backup. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs; a file that can’t be read is listed as such, without Restore); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go; private windows and their tabs are left alone; Favorites over 12 go to Today (D33). When the sidebar can’t be backed up first, nothing changes. A running import stops first: none of the tabs it hasn’t shown yet go to the Archive, and its window says why (D65). Each restore is one step on the sidebar’s undo stack (TB-18): the toast’s Undo or ⌘Z, also in the Library, puts back the sidebar it replaced, a second ⌘Z goes further back and ⌘⇧Z restores again; earlier steps stay. After an undo, a window moved off a removed Space stays where it went, and the pages come back asleep. A folder that comes back with its tabs draws its row in the frame they first show, above them

Only with somewhere to go, and on macOS only with the system's Swipe between pages on. The page gets the swipe first: while what's under the pointer (or around it) can still scroll that way, or the page uses the wheel (preventDefault), the swipe is the page's until the fingers lift, so it navigates only at the scroll edge. Over the sidebar the same swipe switches Space (SP-08) and never navigates. Not offered over a Peek's, a Mini Window's or a pop-up's page, where the swipe does nothing (the spec doesn't say). Windows and Linux: wherever the touchpad scrolls smoothly (pixel deltas); a mouse wheel's notches never navigate. Recognition follows the Space swipe (FL-13): 9 px decide the axis, and the fingers have lifted after a 90 ms pause or when the OS momentum starts. Limits: Electron reports no scroll phases, so the page preload watches the page's wheel events in its own world (D40 use orbit-page:swipe); the swipe goes by the scroll's direction, so with macOS's natural scrolling off a swipe right is forward; a swipe that starts over a frame of the page stays the frame's (frames get no preload); the arrow's small view takes the wheel if the pointer is right over it. Tests use synthetic trackpad scrolls; the real gesture, with momentum, is unverified on macOS (person-check)

Differences: window.print() returns at once and the page's script goes on (Chromium's waits for the dialog), but what would take the page away waits for the dialog: its window.close() (a receipt written into a pop-up or a new tab, printed and closed at once) and a link, location or reload it starts go on once the dialog closes, as they would have (the same address and kind of history entry); a print() while a dialog that ⌘P or a menu opened shows returns at once and holds nothing, as Chromium's does (D76); missing: a form the page posts, or a move through history (history.back(), go()), right after print() goes at once and takes the dialog with it (the engine doesn't let a page's history move be stopped, and posting a form again would run the page's submit handlers twice); a frame's own window.print() opens the system's print dialog (frames have no preload, D40); missing: paper size, margins, scale, pages per sheet and two-sided choices (the preview and PDF are A4, or Letter where the region uses it; a printer uses its own paper); a page may call print() again as soon as its dialog closes. Tests print and save nothing (the one function that sends a job out records it, and the printers come from ORBIT_E2E_PRINTERS); only a person can check that a real printer prints what the preview shows, and Save as PDF's save dialog

NV-12.note: native menu: page (Back, Forward, Reload, Save Page As: complete for a local page, else as a single file or its HTML alone, so no local file a web page or web frame names is copied, D49; Print, View Page Source), link (New Tab, which toasts Opened in a new tab while the sidebar is hidden; Split View, New Window, Private Window, Copy, Save Link As; a local file link or image on a page that is not a local file keeps only its Copy items, D49; a script, page source or data link has no open items), selection (Copy, Search engine, Look Up on macOS), image, video and audio (Loop and Show Controls, ticked as the element is, greyed where the engine cannot: an audio player keeps its controls; then the media lane Picture in Picture on a video), editable (suggestions, Add to Dictionary, edit roles, Paste and Match Style, Writing Direction), Inspect last; Peek and Mini Window items come from their lanes; media items in a frame inside the page act on the frame element playing the same source; P2 Translate and Share Quote not built

NV-13.note: a main-frame load that fails shows Orbit's screen over that page's area only (a tab, a split pane, a Peek, a Mini Window, a pop-up): an icon, a title, one plain sentence in Chromium's words, the site, the engine's error code and Try again, which has the keyboard when the page had it (never taken from the sidebar or the command bar); it is a view over the engine's own error page rather than an orbit: page (D39), so the address keeps the failed URL and ⌘R, Try again, Back and history stay the engine's; a host that doesn't resolve, a refused connection, no internet, an empty response and other net errors each say what happened; the screen stays through a retry that fails again; the row keeps its title and icon when the site that failed is the one it showed, and otherwise shows that site's name (and its icon if Orbit knows one); Orbit gives up on a server that hasn't answered within 120 s (Chromium waits until the user stops it): "took too long to respond", the address stays where it was going, Try again and ⌘R ask again, and Back shows the page before as it was, its screen included; a form being sent is never stopped (it may be uploading); certificates: "Your connection is not private" with Back to safety on the keyboard (back, or closing a tab with nowhere to go back to), Proceed only behind Advanced and never for a revoked certificate, remembered for that certificate and host per profile until Orbit quits; offline: when the network comes back while the screen shows, the page loads again, once (e2e dispatch the engine's online event, as the emulation is per page); a site that asks for HTTPS only (HSTS) still gets Proceed: Electron doesn't say which sites do; gap, as DL-12's (D54): no Safe Browsing interstitial, which needs a reputation service none is free to use; the http not-secure icon is SB-04

NV-14.note: a page that crashes or is killed shows "This page crashed" over its area, with the reason (out of memory, killed…) and Reload, which has the keyboard when the page had it; Reload, ⌘R and ⌘⇧R bring the page back, and closing the tab works as ever; the row keeps its title and icon; a page that crashed behind another shows its crash screen when its row is selected, until the user reloads it (it no longer reloads by itself when shown: the review F11 test in core.spec.ts now reloads it); the same screen shows over a Peek's, a Mini Window's or a pop-up's page (e2e cover tabs); a page that stops responding (the engine's own signal, after about 15 s of unanswered input) gets "Page unresponsive" over it with Wait (Enter, Esc) or Close page, which ends the page's process: its screen then says "This page was closed" with Reload, and other tabs that share that process end too, as in Chromium; the dialog goes by itself when the page answers again; after Wait, a page that stays hung isn't asked about again until it answers and hangs anew (the engine says it once); e2e: the engine says nothing of a hang while a debugger is attached, and Playwright attaches to every page, so the hang tests keep a page really busy and emit the engine's signal; TB-16 (busy background tabs paused) and EX-13 (crashing extensions) are their own rows

NV-15.note: prompt under the address display, as wide as it (over the page's top-left while the sidebar is hidden), for the shown tab or else a split view pane that waits: camera, mic, location, notifications, clipboard, MIDI, idle, windows, fonts, local network, serial/USB/HID choosers, screen share, file access; Allow while visiting / Allow this time / Never allow, or Block / Allow; a press answers only once the prompt has shown for 500 ms and 500 ms after the press before; Esc dismisses; kept per profile and site (private in memory); a frame from another site can't ask for notifications or use the page's; pages read undecided as default/prompt (a PermissionStatus change event doesn't fire for a decision made in Orbit, and the patched getters and requestPermission show their source to toString); a notification click brings its tab forward (page notifications, not service-worker ones; only from a frame allowed notifications, once per 500 ms); Peek, Mini Window and pop-ups ask in a dialog over their own window (Allow, Block, Not Now; Esc keeps nothing; the same request asks once); screen sharing asks only in the screen chooser, never first as camera and microphone (MD-11); a prompt whose view crashed leaves the window, and the keyboard with the page, until its page has loaded again, then shows again (chrome fix check 4, N4); the recording indicators are TB-15's; toolbar anchor waits on SB-17, Site settings is ST-13

NV-16.note: button at the address's right end and the Site Controls action (never shows the hidden sidebar): host and connection, switches for permissions the site used or asked for (pop-ups too), devices, automatic Picture in Picture for the site (MD-08), zoom with reset, Reset permissions, Clear cookies and site data, Reload hint; Esc or a click outside closes; Peek, Developer mode, Tweaks, extensions, capture and the all-sites link wait on their features

NV-18.note: summary of MW-02/05/09/10/11: links from other apps open a Mini Window or follow routing rules, else a Today tab in the most recent Space; never in a private window (e2e); a launch with --private-window takes its links to a private window (NV-11); rules UI is ST-09, Archive restores AR-05

NV-19.note: a link to another app (mailto:, tel:, zoommtg:…) asks first, in a dialog over the page that followed it (a tab's, a split pane's, a Peek's, a Mini Window's or a pop-up's): "Open Mail?" with the app's icon where the OS gives one (macOS, Windows; Linux names the app from its desktop entry and gives no icon), "<site> wants to open this application." naming the site of the frame that followed it, and "Always allow <site> to open links of this type in the associated app" (web sites only; kept per profile, site and kind of link, a private window's in memory only; such a link opens the app without asking once per user gesture in the page, as in Chromium: a page that follows it again before the next click or key in any of its frames opens nothing); Cancel is the default (the keyboard starts there; Enter and Esc give it); an app the OS can't name gets "Open this link in another app?"; on macOS and Windows a kind of link no app opens gets a toast instead of the dialog (not in e2e: test runs give the OS's apps through ORBIT_E2E_APPS); a tab, Peek, Mini Window or pop-up opened only for such a link (target=_blank, window.open, or a redirect there) closes itself once its navigation ends, the tab it came from is selected again, and nothing goes to the Archive; the launch is one function (launchInApp, shell.openExternal) that test runs replace with a recorder, so no test starts an app; schemes Chromium never hands to the OS (shell:, vbscript:, ms-msdt:…) never launch; a page asks one question at a time, and once it has asked, whatever the answer (Open, Cancel or Esc), it asks again only after a new click or key in it, as in Chromium (D77): a link it follows before then gets nothing (a click or a key in any of its frames counts, a frame from another site's too); an Always allow can't be undone in Orbit's UI yet (Site settings has no row for it): deleting the profile forgets it

NV-20.note: ⌃⌘F on macOS (fn+F / Globe+F is the system's own key and does the same), F11 and Alt+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, View → Toggle Full Screen (macOS) and the command bar toggle window full screen; a held key toggles once. In full screen the sidebar hides and the page fills the window; the window's left edge brings the sidebar in over the page (SB-12), and the loading indicator stays (SB-28). Leaving docks the sidebar again, unless the user docked or hid it meanwhile (⌘S); a window closed or quit in full screen keeps its docked sidebar for next time; a window opened from one in full screen opens in full screen, its sidebar hidden (NV-10). Esc in a page, or over its error or crash screen, goes to the page first and full screen stays; pressed again within a second, or held (at its first repeat), it leaves full screen, and the page gets neither that press nor its repeats (nor, as the engine does after a key it didn't deliver, the release); presses further apart each go to the page. A single Esc never leaves, even one the page left alone: nothing asks the page (D60), and a web app's Esc is often its own without preventDefault. Exit Full Screen in Settings → Shortcuts prefers websites by default; set to prefer Orbit, one Esc leaves at once and the page gets nothing of it (KS-02, D68). Esc is no binding of it: an open overlay (command bar, Peek, find bar, a page dialog) takes Esc first (KS-19). The Esc that leaves full screen on a loading page doesn't stop the load (NV-04). A video's own full screen is Chromium's: it fills the window without the sidebar, Esc leaves only it, and the toggle keys leave both. Mini Windows don't go full screen this way. Xvfb has no window manager, so the e2e tests check the state and layout Orbit keeps; a person checks that the window really fills the screen, the macOS animation (the sidebar goes and comes back as it ends), fn+F / Globe+F, and that the View menu has one full-screen item (macOS may add its own Enter Full Screen beside Orbit's). Known limits (keys lane): with the keyboard in a frame of a loading page, the Esc the page gets stops the load after 250 ms, as only the main frame answers (K5); the first key right after the keyboard moves into a frame can come before that frame says where its keyboard is (K7)

NV-21.note: Save Page As…: ⇧⌘S (Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux; ⌘S is the sidebar's, SB-11), File → Save As… (macOS menu), the command bar's Save Page As… and the page menu's, each showing its live keys (KS-18). The OS save dialog opens from the Downloads folder, named after the page: a web page saves as a single file (MHTML) or, named .html, as its HTML alone; a local page whose frames are all local files saves complete (D49). A Peek's or a Mini Window's page saves itself. View Source is DT-04. On a canvas tab the same command exports the canvas: that comes with EZ-11 (no canvases yet).

NV-17.note: copy button = Cmd+Shift+C (clean URL, Copied toast); one-time shortcut tip when the URL is copied from the command bar; on Windows/Linux a page that uses Ctrl+Shift+C gets it first and a toast offers Copy URL, a second press within a second copies (KS-02)

NV-24.note: alert, confirm and prompt show Orbit's own dialog over that page only (a tab, a split view pane, a Peek, a Mini Window, a pop-up): the sidebar, other tabs and the command bar stay usable, a tab's dialog waits while another tab shows and shows again on return, over a Peek it shows above the find bar there; it takes the keyboard only where the page had it (the find bar, a sidebar field such as a tab being renamed, and the address field keep theirs until the user clicks the dialog or the keyboard goes back to the page, D72), Enter answers, Esc cancels (closes an alert), Tab stays in the dialog, and the page gets the keyboard back; the page's text shows as text, cut at 10,000 characters; the title names the asking page's site ("<host> says"), and an about:blank tab or pop-up that its opener writes into names the opener's, as in Chromium; "Leave site?" ("Reload site?" for a reload) when a page that asks for it, from its main frame or a frame (one from another site too), after a user gesture in any of its frames as in Chromium (a click, or a key that reaches the page, a shortcut that goes to the page first included, such as Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Shift+C on Windows and Linux by default; a shortcut Orbit takes first is none, so ⌘W is none unless it is set to go to websites first, D77), goes: a link, a form or location, Orbit's address, Back, Forward or Reload (Leave starts it again), closing its tab (shown first; Cancel keeps it), closing its window or deleting its Space (each page shows as it asks; Cancel keeps the window or the Space, and a page that went before it sleeps), a pop-up's window; a close goes through the engine, which runs every frame's beforeunload only once the close has started (D73); a page's own history.back() or a frame's navigation it stopped goes on at the user's next try within 10 s; auto-archive and sleep let a page go the same way and keep it, without asking, when it warns, or while it waits on its dialog, and don't try it again until it navigates or gets a new user gesture; known limits (D77): the engine's close runs a page's beforeunload with a user activation, which a page that auto-archive or sleep keeps then holds (Orbit's pop-up rule and links to other apps go by Orbit's own count, not the engine's), and ⌘W on a page that has had a user gesture and has a beforeunload listener, while its script is busy, waits for the engine's answer, up to its 1 s limit while no DevTools client is attached to the page (with DevTools open on it, the engine waits out the page's whole busy run), before the tab goes; HTTP sign-in (Basic, Digest; a server or a proxy) over the page, Cancel shows the server's own page; file, folder, colour and date pickers are the engine's own (not run in tests: they wait for a person); a dialog a frame asks for is Electron's: alert and confirm in its own message box, not over the page, which blocks the whole window and not only the tab (a known limit), and prompt returns null (the preload runs in main frames only, D40); quitting doesn't ask; closing a Peek or a Mini Window doesn't ask yet (their close paths are the finish-views lane's)

KS-08.note: Back, Forward, Reload, hard reload, Stop, find (Cmd+F, Cmd+G, Shift+Cmd+G, F3, Ctrl+G), Cmd+J and zoom keys done; full screen ⌃⌘F (F11, Alt+Shift+F) with NV-20; print ⌘P (Ctrl+P) with NV-07; view source ⌥⌘U (Ctrl+U) with DT-04; save page ⇧⌘S (Ctrl+Shift+S) with NV-21. Missing: reader mode ⌥⌘R comes with NV-23 (not built), developer mode ⌃D with DT-06

KS-09.note: ⌃⇧= adds a pane the command bar fills, ⌃⇧− closes the focused pane, ⌃⇧1–4 focus a pane, ⌃⇧] / ⌃⇧[ the next / previous pane (Ctrl+Shift on Windows/Linux), ⌘L / Ctrl+L changes the focused pane's address (SV-15), Add Right/Left/Above/Below Split from the command bar; tested from a page

FL-15.note: every icon button presses to 0.94 at once and springs back (pop), the Library button too; Back/Forward nudge, Reload's glyph turns once, the + scales to 0.92; restarts on repeat; none when disabled; no spring with reduced motion

FL-23.note: after 150 ms, a 48x4 theme-accent pill sweeping on a 1.2 s cycle (a pulse with reduced motion); on load end it fills (80 ms) and fades (150 ms), gone 180 ms after; never moves page content

FL-02.note: 260 ms standard curve drives the sidebar column and the card margins together; interruptible; reduced motion snaps; starts a frame along, so the frame that draws ⌘S already moves

FL-03.note: 0 ms dwell; card in 200 ms (snappy), out 160 ms (quick); hysteresis band; re-entering while it leaves brings it back

AP-05.note: private windows are near-black whatever the theme (frame, sidebar, window background) with hover and selection tuned for black; Private label with icon in the sidebar, not over the page; no Space switcher or Favorites

MD-01.note: Orbit's own floating player: leaving a tab whose main video plays (tab, Space or split change; the largest playing video, in the page or in any of its frames, cross-site ones included) moves it there within ~300 ms, still playing; not when paused, muted or turned off (MD-08); selecting the tab again puts it back in the page (or its frame) with no blank frame, at any load (a frame's page does it from its own size, before its first frame back is drawn); moving between a split's panes doesn't float it. A frame inside a shadow tree can't be found from its page: its video plays on in the tab and in the sidebar controller instead. Known limit (D71): a page's own picture-in-picture button inside a frame returns to the tab without raising the window; the tab is selected only when its window already has focus, in the Space it shows, and once for each frame document (D74). Known limit (D74): a page can end its own picture-in-picture once with exitPictureInPicture() and bring the window forward, as the engine's Back to tab button does; moving it to another of its videos brings nothing forward. Known limit (D78): while a frame's video is in the player, the frame's page can see a hidden div the size of its viewport under <html>, which the frame's script watches, with the root element, to put the video back before the frame is drawn; when the frame's own script, not main, puts a same-site frame's video back, the page may get one "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications" error event, and then its own observers of <html> or <body> get the final size a frame later, as they did before

MD-02.note: Picture in Picture in a video's page right-click menu, the Picture in Picture action and the tray's PiP button; while the tab stays selected the engine's own PiP window shows the video (Orbit's player needs the tab's view), so its controls are the engine's until the tab is left and Orbit's player takes over

MD-03.note: frameless, always-on-top window, 320x180 for 16:9 (keeps the video's shape), bottom-right 16 px inside the work area; rounded corners (a window shape where the system has none) and shadow; video only until hovered, then controls over a dark gradient; the same player on every platform

MD-04.note: on hover: play/pause, +/-15 s, progress with elapsed and total time (seekable; LIVE badge for streams), Back to tab (selects it in its window and Space), x (keeps playing in the sidebar), ... menu (playback speed, turn off today / always for the site), previous/next for Media Session pages; double-click goes back to the tab

MD-05.note: with the player focused (clicked) Space plays and pauses and the arrow keys seek 5 s, its buttons 15 s (tested); hardware media keys reach the playing video through Chromium's media key handling, which Orbit turns on: only a person can check them (no media keys under Xvfb)

MD-06.note: drag or two-finger hover-scroll moves it and it glides to the corner the release or fling heads for; corner drag resizes keeping the shape, at least 200 px wide (tall videos too) and at most half the screen width and the screen's height, with rubber-band resistance; Cmd/Ctrl+scroll or pinch zooms (crops) inside the window; corner and size remembered. While an Orbit window shows an alert or dialog (the engine disables the window meanwhile, macOS shows a sheet, and Orbit's own file pickers and save dialogs say so; so do Orbit's dialogs and screens over a page while they show: a page's alert, confirm, prompt and "Open Mail?", the print dialog, and the error, crash and "Page unresponsive" screens), the player keeps clear of where it shows, up to 900 x 620 centered on the window (from its top on macOS): it glides to the nearest clear corner at its size, or goes out of sight, still playing, when no corner is clear, and comes back when the dialog closes unless it was moved meanwhile; its remembered place doesn't change (tested with an alert, and with a page's confirm, the print dialog and a crash screen). A web page's own file picker on Linux isn't seen: the engine doesn't disable the window for it

MD-07.note: returning (select, double-click, Back to tab) ends it with the video playing in the page; x closes it and the media keeps playing in the sidebar controls; closing or unloading the tab stops media and player; navigating the tab or the video ending closes it, without replay; a picture-in-picture the engine closes because another one opened (in another pane, tab or window, by a page or by Orbit) isn't Back to tab: nothing is selected and no window comes forward (D75)

MD-08.note: site controls panel (NV-16) Picture in Picture switch, on by default: off is Always turn off for this site, on undoes it and Turn off for today, which it shows too; player ... menu Turn Off for Today / Always Turn Off for This Site (also in the tray controller menu); global switch Settings > Advanced (ST-10) and the Picture in Picture action; turning off keeps playback (sidebar controls); muted tabs never trigger

MD-09.note: controller above the bottom bar: the Media Session's artwork (loaded with the tab's session, kept small) or the favicon, Media Session title/artist or tab title (marquee), play/pause, next, previous where supported, x pauses and hides; click jumps to the tab (switching Space); quiet audio counts; hidden while its tab is selected; media in frames (embedded players, cross-site too) has the same controls

MD-10.note: one controller per background tab, newest first, appears and disappears by itself, works across windows; a video's controller has Picture in Picture (Back to PiP): the player grows out of the controller while the controller gives way

MD-11.note: pulsing camera/microphone indicator on tab rows (tracks the page shows); a distinct blue screen-share indicator, lit while either source says a share is live (D69): main's watcher, put in the asking frame (any frame) when Orbit's screen chooser grants, or the page preload's count of the main frame's live shared tracks (covers macOS 15's system picker); only chooser grants keep a tab awake and unarchived; known limit: a page that wants to hide its share can (e.g. clone a track with a same-origin frame's built-ins and stop the one Orbit follows), the OS's own indicator is the backstop; a frame's share the macOS 15 picker grants doesn't show; a capture that fails after the chooser granted it shows until the page leaves; Peek and Mini Window shares have no row; per-pane Mute/Unmute in the split row's menu (split lane's menu, tested here: only that pane goes silent); the recent-tab switcher (TB-05) shows the same camera/microphone and screen-share indicators, and the sound state, as the rows

MD-12.note: playing (muted too), PiP and camera/mic tabs never sleep, auto-archive, Clear or Archive Below; closing stops media, PiP and controller; isAnyMediaPlaying() is ready for the updates lane

MD-13.note: leaving a call tab floats the largest participant video (never the self view) in Orbit's player with microphone/camera toggles and Back to call tab; moves and resizes like any video (a pinch zooms, as for any video). Not built: leave call (the site's Media Session hang-up handler lives in the page's own script world, which Orbit reaches only through a page patch, a lead decision under D40), a chat toggle (no web API exposes a site's chat), and the site's own document picture-in-picture view (also only through the page's Media Session)

MD-14.note: a background call tab (or a closed call window) gets a sidebar call controller: microphone and camera toggles (track.enabled on the tracks the page shows) and jump back. Not built: a call is seen only when its page shows its own camera (a self view); an audio-only call isn't, because the browser process can't see what a page captures and watching getUserMedia takes a page patch (a lead decision under D40)

MD-15.note: not possible as specified: Orbit's screen chooser shares a screen or a window, never a single tab, and the engine can't change what a running share captures (switching the shared tab is the Chrome browser's own feature, not in Electron); swapping the call page's video track would take a page patch, a lead decision under D40

MD-16.note: enter: the video shrinks from its place in the page to the corner (~300 ms, standard curve); Back to tab/double-click: the tab is selected at once and a still of the last frame flies back into the page; release glides to the corner; Back to PiP grows from the controller; tray slides with the snappy spring; with reduced motion (FL-28) the player appears and goes without motion and a release settles with a 120 ms ease-out. Not possible: a haptic tick on macOS (Electron has no haptics; it would take native code), and fading in the engine's own PiP window, which shows only while the tab stays selected (MD-02). Only a person can check playback for stutter

FL-32.note: corner resize follows the pointer, resists past its limits (rubber band) and springs back on release; a fling heads for the corner in its direction and settles with the spring; tray slides up with the snappy timing; Back to tab flies to the video's place; pinch zooms (MD-06) rather than resizes

KS-11.note: Space and arrows in the focused player, Cmd/Ctrl+scroll and pinch zoom (tested), hardware media keys via Chromium (untested), Mute Tab action assignable; the calendar meeting shortcut (P2) belongs to TB-21/FV-09

KS-12.note: ⌘Y / Ctrl+H View History (AR-10); ⌘⇧L Open Library on macOS, the command bar elsewhere; View Archive with no key, assignable; ⌘, / Ctrl+, Settings, which cannot be remapped, and again brings the same Settings window to the front; ⌘⇧⌫ / Ctrl+Shift+Delete Clear Browsing Data…; Shortcut Settings (command bar, assignable); the shortcut sheet from Help → Keyboard Shortcuts (macOS) and the command bar (OB-12); Open File… (macOS File menu, the command bar) and ⌘O / Ctrl+O wherever no Peek or Mini Window is open: the files chosen open in new tabs, the last one selected (Settings → Shortcuts says so under Open File…, which can also get keys of its own); with no Orbit window shown, the macOS menu bar takes ⌘O itself, so Open File… still opens (F6); Alt+F stays free for the Windows/Linux app menu (SB-03, SB-26, not built). Not built: Open Downloads (DL-14, downloads lane), pinned extensions (EX-06)

A remap reaches DevTools already open only once they open again (devtools lane). KS-10.note: ⌘O / Ctrl+O expands a Peek into a selected Today tab (PK-07); Esc and ⌘W / Ctrl+W close it (PK-09, Esc fixed); ⌘⇧T and ⌘Z reopen it (PK-10); ⌘⌥N / Ctrl+Alt+N opens a Mini Window (MW-06); in a Mini Window ⌘O moves its page into the most recent Space (MW-05), ⌘⌥O (also ⌘⇧O) / Ctrl+Alt+O offers the Spaces, ⌘W closes it (MW-09). All from the one keymap and remappable but Esc; the tests press the keys (peek, mini-window and keys specs)

KS-15.note: macOS: the menu bar keeps the system’s items and keys: Hide Orbit ⌘H, Hide Others ⌥⌘H and Quit ⌘Q in the Orbit menu, the Window menu (Minimize ⌘M, ⌘` between Orbit windows) and the Help menu with its search (⌘?). Full screen: every key works with the sidebar hidden; ⌘1–9 and ⌘⌥↑ / ⌘⌥↓ switch tabs without bringing it out. SB-10.note: media tray and call controls (media lane), above the bottom bar, pushing the list up; download progress and the update banner belong to other lanes

PK-02.note: other-site (eTLD+1) link clicks, Enter on a focused link, and target=_blank in pinned tabs/Favorites; same-site navigates. Only a navigation to the clicked link counts, so form posts, script navigations and auto-posted sign-ins stay in the tab

PK-04.note: meeting links open a tab; routing rules (settings.linkRules) win; rules UI is the settings lane's

PK-05.note: inset card, shadow, dimmed page area, Close / Open as Tab / Split buttons with shortcut tooltips; no toolbar (AP-07 not built)

PK-06.note: spring grow from the link, 18% dim (20% dark), 160 ms shrink to 0.96 and fade, reduced motion; drag the top handle or swipe down beside the card: follows the input, closes past 25% or 500 px/s, else springs back

PK-07.note: ⌘O / button: card morphs to the frame, live page becomes a selected Today tab (routing rules apply)

PK-08.note: the card slides to the right half, then split.addTab makes the source and the live Peek page one split in the source's place (a pinned source gives a pinned split), the page focused; from a full split the Peek stays open and the SV-25 toast shows

PK-09.note: Esc (after fullscreen), ⌘W, ×, click outside; archived as from 'peek'

PK-10.note: ⌘Z right after closing, or ⌘⇧T, reopens on the same page with history

PK-11.note: links, forms, back/forward, reload, zoom, copy URL and copy URL as Markdown, print, devtools and find in page act on the Peek: ⌘F, ⌘G and F3 bring the find bar over the Peek card's top-right corner, searching the Peek's page with its own search, and Esc gives the Peek the keyboard back; a dialog the Peek's page asks for shows above the find bar, which keeps the keyboard it has until it closes (D72); the tab under it keeps its own search; the sidebar address shows the Peek host; ⌘L makes it a tab and edits it; downloads go to the normal list (DL-16). Not built: extensions in Peek pages come with EX-11

PK-12.note: Settings → Links has both toggles ("Open links from pinned tabs and Favorites in Peek", "Shift-click opens links in Peek"), on by default on every platform; off, a pinned tab's or Favorite's other-site link opens as a Today tab and ⇧-click opens a new window. Tests: settings.spec ST-09/MW-11 (toggles, defaults), peek.spec PK-12, nav-links.spec NV-08 ⇧-click, link-routing unit PK-12

PK-13.note: no sidebar row; sidebar stays usable; selecting another tab, Space or window dismisses (reopenable)

PK-15.note: no hover-to-Peek trigger: hovering links or pinned rows never opens a Peek (hover cards are TB-21)

PK-16.note: Mini Window links never Peek; target=_blank stays in the Mini Window

FL-19.note: open: a spring tuned to FL-19's 280–320 ms (response 0.275 s, ratio 0.92; the standard token FL-19 names takes longer over a card's travel, D70), within 2 px in ~320 ms with no overshoot, 18% dim; expand meets the frame in ~250 ms, then the row enters; split slides to the right half; close 160 ms to 0.96 + fade, the page behind takes clicks again 173–194 ms after Escape (best of up to three rounds, at the edge of 200 ms); drag/swipe dismiss; ⌘Z/⌘⇧T replay the open

FL-24.note: Library opens with a 220 ms fade and 0.98→1 scale (opacity only with reduced motion) and fades out; sections cross-fade in 90 ms; search answers within 50 ms; restored rows fade and the rows below rise; long lists virtualised; a previewed entry opens and closes with the Peek's motion (FL-19)

MW-01.note: separate small window, one floating tab, main window untouched

MW-02.note: open-url / second-instance / argv links open a Mini Window; same URL resurfaces it; routing rules first

MW-03.note: slim top bar: controls, favicon+host (click/⌘L opens the compact command bar on the page's address, CB-23), Open in…, profile pill; inset page card; neutral theme. ⌘F opens a find field in the top bar beside the host (NV-05): finds as you type, n/m count, No matches, Enter/⌘G/F3 next and ⇧ for previous, buttons; Esc closes it, keeps the match selected and gives the page the keyboard; keys typed before the field has the keyboard are not held (as they are for the main window's bar)

MW-04.note: a quick scale-and-fade instead of the OS's animation: the window's UI grows from 92% to full size in 200 ms (the --ease-out curve) in its own layer while the window fades in (macOS, Windows; Linux can't fade a window, so there the UI fades in too). The OS window is not resized, which would lay the page out every frame: the page's native view, loading all along, sits out the grow and joins on the card at full size when it ends. Reduced motion shows it at once. Opens at the last-used size and place, each further window 24 px down and right; on macOS it shows above a full-screen Orbit window, on the current desktop. Only a person can check the desktop and full-screen parts, on a Mac

MW-05.note: ⌘O to the most recent Space, Open in… / ⌘⌥O (⌘⇧O) native Space menu; live page, no reload

MW-06.note: ⌘⌥N opens a pre-rendered blank window with a focused lookup bar, the command bar's compact variant (CB-23): history and typed-text rows, inline completion, site search, engine suggestions; the choice loads here; Esc empties it, Esc on the empty bar or ⌘W closes the window. System-wide on macOS only (outside e2e); on Windows/Linux Ctrl+Alt+N works inside Orbit, so other apps (and AltGr+N) keep the key

MW-07.note: ⌘⌥-click a link, link menu Open Link in Mini Window, or ⌘⌥-click a sidebar row: Today rows move live, pinned/Favorite rows open a copy

MW-08.note: any number; Show/Hide All action and macOS dock menu

MW-09.note: close and idle auto-close (settings.miniWindowArchiveAfterMs, 6 h, 0 = never; not while audible) archive with from 'mini'

MW-10.note: profile pill/menu reopens the page in another profile; remembered per site

MW-11.note: settings.miniWindowForExternalLinks off: tabs in the most recent or chosen Space (externalLinksSpace)

MW-12.note: a video's full screen happens in the Mini Window: the window fills the screen with the page, which stays there, and the card comes back on exit (tested); copy URL, devtools, downloads through the profile's session. Not built: extensions (Orbit has no extension support yet, EX-11), captures saved to a canvas (no Canvases yet) and sharing (Orbit has no share feature)

MW-13.note: off by default; Settings > General > Mini Window turns it on: Orbit's mark as a template glyph in the macOS menu bar, the app's icon in the Windows and Linux tray (the drawn mark where a build has no icon file); a click opens a blank Mini Window with its lookup bar focused (macOS: right-click for its menu); its menu has New Mini Window and Show/Hide All Mini Windows, New Mini Window first for Linux trays that show only the menu (tested through the button's click and menu). GNOME shows tray icons only with an AppIndicator extension; on Windows and Linux Orbit still quits with its last window, button or not

MW-14.note: all platforms with Ctrl+Alt+N / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+Alt+O, in-app outside macOS (D23), with the tray button (MW-13) as the way in from other apps; New Mini Window and Show/Hide All in the macOS dock menu, the Windows jump list, Linux launcher actions and the tray menu. Launcher actions: a packaged Linux folder build writes ~/.local/share/applications/<name>.desktop at start-up (under $XDG_DATA_HOME when that is set; <name> is Electron's desktop name), with no opt-out for now, and keeps it pointing at where Orbit runs from. It never touches an entry a package installed, one the user wrote, or one it can't read (checked on a packaged build: both actions reach the running Orbit). Only a person can check the Windows jump list

MW-15.note: warm spare window takes keys at once, page loads before the window shows; opens with MW-04's 200 ms grow and fade; Open in… shrinks to 92% and fades (140 ms, macOS/Windows) as the row enters Today

DL-09.note: Library container (archive lane): section list on the left with the Archive, History (AR-10) and Backups (AR-11) sections; other lanes add theirs through the registry. Reopens to the last section; Esc/⌘W close and the previous tab comes back. Its view is made once Orbit is idle after launch, so even the first open is quick (about 70 ms at 10,000 entries; later opens 10–50 ms). Downloads lane: the Media and Downloads sections (just before Downloads, Media); right after a download, a closed Library opens on Downloads next time; their items open in a Peek over the Library (⌘/Ctrl-click: a tab). Missing, all owned by other lanes: Canvases & Notes (notes lane), Spaces (finish-tabs, SP-13) and Site customizations (tweaks, BO-15)

DL-01.note: per-profile sessions save to the profile's folder (OS Downloads), name (1) on collisions, .crdownload until done; a blank tab opened for a download closes; outlives its page; quitting asks while downloads run

DT-01.note: ⌥⌘I / F12 (Ctrl+Shift+I / F12) open DevTools for the selected tab or focused split pane, docked inside its view, and close them, also from inside DevTools; a Peek's or Mini Window's page gets its own. ⌥⌘J (Ctrl+Shift+J) opens them on the Console; View → Developer menu (macOS) and the command bar. A key held down acts once. Copy, paste (after DevTools' own paste warning) and the device toolbar work; links DevTools open become tabs. Windows/Linux: while DevTools have the keyboard, only the DevTools keys reach Orbit

DT-02.note: right-click → Inspect (last item) opens DevTools with that element selected, or just selects it when they're open. Picker: ⌥⌘C on macOS, no default key on Windows/Linux, Inspect Element in the command bar. ⇧⌘C stays Copy URL; inside DevTools it is DevTools' own picker. Remap: give the devtools.inspect action ⇧⌘C (and take it from tab.copyUrl) in src/shared/actions.ts, or in Settings → Shortcuts once remapping (ST-08) lands

DT-03.note: docked right/left/bottom or undocked from DevTools' dock menu; the engine keeps the side per profile across restarts. Each tab (pane, Peek, Mini Window) has its own DevTools, shown and hidden with its page; a page shown again takes the docked size last chosen. Undocked: the open key brings them to the front (checked on Linux; macOS unverified), and closes them when they have the keyboard. No windows added, however many tabs have DevTools. What Orbit puts over a page (find bar, zoom, link pill, loading indicator, permission prompt) goes over the page's own area, never over docked DevTools (e2e for the find bar and link pill, docked right, bottom and left)

DT-04.note: ⌥⌘U (Ctrl+U), the command bar's View Source, the page menu's View Page Source and View → Developer → View Source (macOS menu) open the page's own address as view-source: in a new tab, shown at once: the engine's source view, read-only, coloured, with line numbers; a Peek's page opens its own source in a new tab of its window, and a Mini Window's in a main window (one showing its Space if there is one), brought to the front; a source view has no source of its own to open. Only the page's own address goes, so a web page can't make Orbit open a file: URL this way (D49)

DT-13.note: orbit://<page>/ opens as a normal tab when typed in the command bar or address field, or from another internal page's link; orbit://pages/ lists them; orbit://version/ shows the build info About shows (Orbit, build day, Electron, Chromium, V8, Node, OS) with Copy build info. orbit://history/ is History (AR-10, pages lane). They follow the app's state (light/dark) through the same bridge as Orbit's UI, which the one web page preload (src/preload/page.ts) gives an orbit: page's main frame only (D40, D53). A web page can't navigate, frame, redirect to, open, load or fetch them, and gets no bridge: Orbit opens one for no page but another internal page on any route (the page menu, Split View's item included, ⌥-click, new tabs, windows and pop-ups, a pop-up's own, blocked pop-ups, a drop), D53. Each page runs only the commands listed for it and sends no events, and its document runs only its own scripts (script-src 'self'), D53. Infrastructure documented for reuse (D39) in src/main/devtools/internal-pages.ts and src/renderer/src/internal/registry.ts: a page is a *.internal-page.tsx module, and lists the commands it runs in INTERNAL_PAGE_COMMANDS. Missing: the pages other lanes add as they build them (D54): extensions EX-07, site settings OT-07/ST-13, privacy and clearing data and system options ST-12, languages ST-14, about UP-07; orbit://pages/ lists each one added

DT-14.note: ⇧⌘R (Ctrl+Shift+R) runs the navigation lane's nav.hardReload action (the e2e checks that action ran): page and subresources refetched (no-cache). A crashed page hands the keyboard to the window, so ⇧⌘R brings it back. Stopping a load (Esc in the page, double-clicking Reload) is NV-04, built with the sidebar's Reload/Stop button; its e2e tests cover both

DL-02.note: a file icon flies from the page's edge into the Library button (≈0.5 s curved path, ease-out) and the button bounces; one flight per download; reduce motion: a fade on the button. Sidebar hidden: a "Downloading <file>" toast (and "Downloaded"/"Couldn't download"). A Mini Window's downloads show in its main window

DL-03.note: row above the bottom bar: name truncated in the middle, progress bar, bytes of total, time left (smoothed), ✕ cancels and deletes the partial file; several: newest + "+N", hover or "+N" lists each with its own ✕; done for 4 s, click opens; failed: Resume or Retry, ✕ dismisses; no downloads, no room taken. Right-click: the download's menu

DL-04.note: Open (in an Orbit tab only types that run no script there, D53: PDF, raster images, plain text, audio, video; anything else, SVG and HTML included, in the system app), Show in Finder / Show in Folder, Copy File (pastes as the file in file managers), Copy Download Link, Remove from List, Delete File; these act on whatever file is at the download's path, also one edited since (D56). Only with no file there (moved away or deleted), or once a later download saved its file there, the row shows "File Missing" and Download Again. The same menu on the sidebar row, the Library's Downloads rows (right-click or ⋯), the recent-files popover and the flyout. Missing: Open with…, which finish-downloads builds (D54)

DL-07.note: Settings → Profiles → [profile] → Download location: a dropdown with the profile's folder (its full path under it), Other… (the OS folder picker) and Ask every time; per profile, a new one starts with the OS Downloads folder. Ask every time shows the OS save dialog for each download, opening in the folder the last one went to (kept across restarts; a private window's choice isn't kept); the file downloads meanwhile under a hidden name where the dialog opens and moves into place when complete (a copy across disks); it shows in the sidebar and the lists once placed, and Cancel drops it. A chosen folder is always used, never the one last used with Ask every time; a folder that can't be written to (a drive that's gone) asks with the save dialog and says why, never saving elsewhere silently. Tests answer the dialogs through test hooks

DL-08.note: Remove from List keeps the file; Delete File moves it to the Trash/Recycle Bin (never a permanent delete; stays listed and says so when it can't), only while it is the file downloaded (same size and date, D56): one edited since, or another at its path, stays where it is with the download listed, and a toast says it changed after it was downloaded; Clear all, in the Library's Downloads section, takes finished downloads off the list (files stay; the partial file of a failed one goes) and keeps running, paused, held (DL-12) and resumable ones. Missing: the "Download history" choice in Clear browsing data, which finish-settings builds (ST-12, D54); it can call downloads.clear with the profile

DL-15.note: Pause/Resume from the row's menu (and a Resume button on a paused row); a cut-off download shows Resume when the server sent an ETag or Last-Modified (continues with a range request), else Retry (starts again); one cut off by quitting resumes after a restart from its partial file (kept under a hidden second name while the engine shuts down). Downloads never block the tab that started them

DL-16.note: Peek and Mini Window downloads go to the same list as any other. A private window's downloads save to disk like any other but are in no saved list (not the downloads list, nor the state file or its backup), and their Windows Zone.Identifier names no address. A private window shows only its own session's downloads (sidebar row, Ctrl+J flyout), and no other window shows them; their start, toasts and the files Orbit opens stay in its windows, and they change nothing kept (the Library's section, the Dock's notification names no file). They stay listed while a private window is open, its pages closed or not; when the last one closes (the session ends), they leave every list: finished files stay on disk, one still coming is saved and then leaves, a paused or stopped one and a program held back (DL-12) are discarded. Tested with real private windows

DL-17.note: While downloads run or are paused, their overall progress shows on the macOS Dock icon and on the windows' taskbar buttons: bytes received of those with a known size, the can't-tell bar when no size is known, Windows' paused colour when every one is paused; it goes when none runs. A download that finishes while no Orbit window has focus bounces the Dock icon once (macOS) and shows a "Download complete" notification naming the file (a private window's isn't named). Tests read what Orbit asks of the OS through test hooks; the OS's own drawing isn't checked on Linux

DL-05.note: hovering the Library button 300 ms shows a popover above it, inside the sidebar: the 8 newest downloads (and OS screenshots when chosen), each with its picture or kind icon, name, size and age; a click opens one, dragging drops the file (DL-06), right-click shows its menu; it goes 200 ms after the pointer leaves. Right-click the button: Recent Files with Downloads and Screenshots checkboxes (Downloads on, Screenshots off at first) and Show Screenshots in Library (DL-11). No Captures choice: Orbit has no capture tool (OT-03)

DL-06.note: every download drags out as the real file (the OS drag, with a file icon): the sidebar row, the recent-files popover, the Library's Downloads rows and Media tiles, and the Ctrl+J flyout (which steps aside once the drag ends). Tests stop at the OS drag (Xvfb can't drop). Not verified by hand: dropping into the page under the flyout, and dragging while Orbit is in the background on macOS (an inactive window takes the first click unless it accepts the first mouse, a window-wide choice). Missing: dropping into a canvas (EZ-05), which the canvases lane builds

DL-10.note: Library → Downloads: everything downloaded through Orbit in the profile (running ones too, wherever saved; nothing else from the folder), newest first in day groups; a row shows a picture or kind icon, name, size or progress, site and time; search by name (every word, any case); a click previews in a Peek over the Library (PDF, images, text, audio, video; other files open in their app), ⌘/Ctrl-click opens a tab; hover buttons Show in Finder/Folder, Resume, Retry, Cancel, Keep/Discard and ⋯ for the full menu (DL-04, DL-08); rows drag out (DL-06); arrow keys and Enter; a profile switcher when there are several profiles; Clear all. Only the rows on screen are drawn

DL-11.note: Library → Media: a grid of the pictures and videos downloaded in the profile (those Orbit can show), newest first by day; video tiles play muted and looping while on screen (still with reduced motion); a click opens a larger preview in a Peek (⌘/Ctrl-click: a tab), tiles drag out as the file, right-click shows the file's menu. Right-click the Library button → Show Screenshots in Library adds the OS screenshots (macOS: the system's screenshot folder, else the Desktop; Windows: Pictures\Screenshots; Linux: Pictures/Screenshots and screenshot-named files in Pictures). Out of scope (D54): in-browser captures, which need OT-03, a feature with no spec row

DL-12.note: finished files carry the OS mark of a file from the internet (the macOS quarantine attribute; on Windows a Zone.Identifier with the page and file address, no passwords, and only the zone for a private window's download; Linux has none). Programs, installers, scripts and disk images wait under their partial name with Keep / Discard in the sidebar row, the Library and the flyout, through a restart too: everywhere exe, msi, dmg, pkg, deb, rpm, AppImage, .desktop launchers, sh/bash/zsh/py/pl/rb scripts, iso/img/vhd/vhdx, jar, jnlp, apk…; on Windows also its own script, shortcut and system types (js, vbs, wsf, hta, lnk, url, scf, settingcontent-ms, chm, reg, inf, msc, dll…). Keep puts the file in place and marks it, Discard deletes it. Every such file is held, whatever the site, as there is no reputation service. Gap, by the spec's own rule (D54): Safe Browsing, which needs a reputation service; none is free to use (Google's is non-commercial, Web Risk is paid)

DL-13.note: PDFs (the engine's viewer), raster pictures, plain text, audio and video open in a tab (only types that run no script there, D53: a downloaded SVG opens in its app); a site that sends the file as an attachment still downloads it (DL-01); the PDF viewer's download button saves through the usual download flow (row, Library, DL-02 flight). Missing: offering Orbit as Windows' app for local .pdf files (Settings → General, P2), which finish-settings builds (D54): the installer's file association and opening files passed on the command line

DL-14.note: Windows/Linux: Ctrl+J opens the downloads flyout at the top left, beside the sidebar (Orbit has no top toolbar): the 12 newest with live progress, Keep/Discard, Resume/Retry/Cancel and Show in Folder; a click opens a file, rows drag out (DL-06), Show All opens the Library's Downloads section; Esc, Ctrl+J again or a click outside closes it. macOS: ⌘⇧J and ⌥⌘L open the Library's Downloads section (KS-12). The command bar has a "Downloads" action

ST-01.note: own window (⌘, / Ctrl+,): opens or focuses one; remembers section and size; takes the opener Space's colours; sections come from a registry (src/renderer/src/settings/registry.ts); search filters rows

ST-02.note: sections and common settings are command-bar actions (settings.*) that open Settings at the row; the keys lane adds Shortcuts

ST-03.note: default browser row, app-menu item and command-bar action (only an installed build can register; e2e uses a stub); Mini Window archive timing; Import… opens the import flow (IM-01); Updates group: automatic checks switch, Check Now and the update feed address. Not built: UP-04's install-while-idle, hover-preview toggles (OT-26, P2), Open PDFs (P2)

ST-04.note: list with Default first, rename any profile, New Profile…, delete with confirmation (off while a Space uses it, and says why)

ST-05.note: 12 hours (default), 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days per profile; no Never; other profiles follow Default until set

ST-06.note: per-profile default engine (8 built-ins), custom engines with keyword and %s URL, Make default from the row menu; no extension override in Electron, so that row does not exist

ST-20.note: per-profile rows carry the profile's name, the download location (DL-07) too; passwords and site permissions don't exist yet

AP-01.note: Light / Dark / Match system in Settings and the Space theme picker; about 200 ms cross-fade, no flash

OB-02.note: audit and e2e: no account UI anywhere, onboarding included; a first run sends nothing off the computer, with or without onboarding, except Chromium's spell-check dictionary download (see tests)

ST-08.note: Settings → Shortcuts: every action Orbit has (the action table, as main registers it) in groups with a search by name, search words or keys; click a key, press the new one (a modifier first except F1–F12; system and reserved keys refused, with the reason, and on macOS ⌃ with a lone letter, which moves the caret in text fields, D60); + adds another (up to 5), ⌫ while listening removes one, Esc cancels; a key another action has asks: Swap (when replacing) or Remove from the other; right-click: Reset to Default, Remove Shortcut, Prefer Websites / Prefer Orbit (KS-02); Reset All asks first; Go to Tab: Include Favorites in ordering and ⌘9 last or ninth item; actions with no keys (Duplicate Tab…) show Record Shortcut; keys the system keeps are marked (KS-03); Settings search finds rows; stored per device; Exit Full Screen (Esc in full screen, NV-20) has its row with no keys of its own, preferring websites by default, and its priority sets Esc's

ST-09.note: links from other apps open in a Mini Window (default), the most recent Space or one Space; routing rules (address contains / is exactly → a Space; first match wins; add, edit, reorder, remove); Peek options

ST-10.note: tab sleep timer (TB-16), picture in picture, graphics acceleration; no site customizations, full-URL toggle, sounds or haptics, or edge-drag settings because those features don't exist yet

ST-12.note: privacy promise (Orbit sends nothing); Clear browsing data per profile (⌘⇧⌫ / Ctrl+Shift+Delete): history by time range; cookies and site data, and the cache, always from all time (Electron has no range), so they start ticked only for All time; Secure DNS (Automatic, Off, Cloudflare, Google, Quad9); graphics acceleration lives in Advanced. No HTTPS-first or Safe Browsing (not in Electron), no per-site clearing here

OB-01.note: a window of its own before any browser window on a first run (gated by settings.onboarded; e2e runs skip it unless ORBIT_ONBOARDING=1): Orbit's logo with the moon in motion (still with reduced motion), a welcome line, Get started; steps slide in (about 400 ms, none with reduced motion); Enter continues, Esc goes back; each step's title takes focus; progress dots are labelled. No sounds or music (optional), no haptics (Electron has no API), no first-window shimmer

OB-03.note: the import flow inline (IM-01 to IM-06): the browsers on this computer, several profiles allowed, the data types and the bookmark tree, a bookmarks file dropped or chosen, the paste route and the help for people moving from another browser, with Do this later weighing the same as Next. An import chosen there is read at once and added when Start browsing ends onboarding, where the Done screen sums it up; Skip setup adds nothing (D44). Letter tiles, not browser logos (as IM-02)

OB-04.note: the Space theme picker (same ThemeEditor) for the first Space, applied live, with a preview of sidebar and frame, grain and intensity; Light / Dark / Match system (Match system preselected, Continue works at once); says it can be changed later. No haptics

OB-05.note: 16 web apps as letter tiles (no logos fetched), nothing preselected, at most 12; they become the first Space's profile's Favorites, unloaded until opened. No ordering by imported history (no import yet)

OB-06.note: there is no ad and tracker blocker (OT-15), so the step is left out of the flow

OB-07.note: explains what the default browser does; Make Orbit my default and Not now with the same weight; on Windows says what to pick in Default apps; status asked again when the window comes back to the front; no reminders later. Test runs use a stub

OB-08.note: a Search with row on the Done screen: the Default profile's engine (ST-06's list), Google until changed

OB-09.note: Done screen sums up colours, Favorites, default browser and import (what will be added from where, e.g. "6 bookmarks from bookmarks.html", or that nothing was and where import lives); Start browsing (Back to browsing after a reset) opens the first window centred at about 86% of the screen with the colours and Favorites picked, command bar closed. No Orbit basics folder or local welcome tab (no local guide pages yet)

OB-14.note: Skip setup on every step but the last gives the spec's default first window: the theme step's colours and mode are undone and no Favorites are added (D44). The step, the theme and the Favorites picked so far are saved, so a quit part-way resumes there with them. An import chosen at the import step isn’t: it waits in memory for Start browsing, so a quit before then loses it, and the Done step says nothing was imported (it’s in Settings, under General); Reset Onboarding (command bar only) runs the flow again over the open windows and deletes nothing

IM-01.note: the import window (a child of the browser window, in its Space's colours): Back / Next / Cancel, Cancel at any step imports nothing, Enter is Next and Escape is Back, ⌘W closes it. IM-02.note: the browsers found on this computer (Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Opera GX, Firefox; Safari on macOS), each a tile in its colour with its profile or profile count; those not installed aren't shown. IM-03.note: after the source and its profiles, what they hold as checkboxes, all on, with counts ("6 bookmarks, as pinned tabs", "6 pages visited"); types a source can't provide aren't shown, and a profile whose file the browser holds offers the rest; never passwords or cards (D52). IM-06.note: the last step: the profile (it gets the history) and the Space (its pinned section gets the bookmarks): the current Space by default, the first one in onboarding, or New Space… with a name. IM-04.note: the source's tree (Chromium's bookmarks bar, other and mobile bookmarks; Firefox's toolbar, menu, other and mobile bookmarks; Safari's favorites bar, menu and reading list; a file's own groups), several profiles each under its name, with a checkbox per folder and bookmark; everything chosen at first; Select all / none; "4 of 6 bookmarks selected". Addresses that can't be pinned show unticked with the reason. Folders below the top level start closed, and so does a top-level one holding over 1,000 bookmarks. The list isn’t virtualized: every row at the top level or in an open folder is drawn, so a large file shows quickly only when its bookmarks sit in such closed folders (20,000 in folders of 2,000 show in about 0.4 s). 20,000 bookmarks at the top level take about 2.9 s to show; 200,000 there, or 200 top-level folders of 1,000, about 30 s; 10,000 top-level folders about 6 s; and opening a large folder draws all its rows. Only the import window waits

IM-05.note: one pinned folder "Imported from <Browser>" ("Imported bookmarks" from a file) at the end of the target Space's pinned section: the source's top-level groups and nested folders kept, in order, as closed sub-folders (the folder itself closed above 1,000 items); several profiles into one Space each get a sub-folder by name; each bookmark a pinned tab with its title and address, asleep, with no favicon or request until opened; bookmarklets, saved searches, browser-only and non-web addresses skipped and counted; Firefox tags and separators left out; no Favorites made; one undo step takes it all back. 2,000 bookmarks take about 0.3–0.4 s, made out of sight in parts and shown at once (IM-14), with the longest main-process stall about 40–50 ms. IM-13.note: bookmarks HTML (the Netscape format; Chromium- and Firefox-style exports tested) and a .txt list of links, from From a file… or dropped on the import window or the sidebar. Bookmarks map as IM-05 into "Imported bookmarks"; links as IM-12 (a list over about 1 MB or 10,000 lines shows only its count and first lines); a file with neither says "No bookmarks found in this file" and imports nothing; a cut-off file imports what it holds. Files are read in a worker, in time linear in their size (D58): main’s longest stall is about 0.07 s for a 16 MB file or list, and about 0.2 s for a 60 MB file of 200,000 bookmarks. A file nested deeper than 64 folders keeps its deeper bookmarks in the 64th; a file gives at most 200,000 bookmarks (folders don’t count) and 20,000 folders, the bookmarks of folders past that kept in the folder that holds them; over 64 MB, every route, a paste included, says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)” without reading it; a read that fails says “Orbit couldn’t read this file”. No passwords CSV (D52)

IM-12.note: Paste a list of links (one address per line, "Title — address" with a dash, bar or tab, Markdown links, bullets): one pinned folder named by the user, a pinned tab per link in order, asleep; lines that aren't links are counted in the summary. ⌘V / Ctrl+V on the sidebar (outside a text field) with two or more links on the clipboard opens the same import with them filled in. A list over about 1 MB or 10,000 lines, pasted or from a file, isn’t put in the text field: the import window shows its count and first eight lines, read-only, with Clear, and imports it as it is. A paste over 64 MB as UTF-8 (22.5 million CJK characters, say) says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)”, as a file does, and none of it leaves the window it was pasted in. Clear also frees main’s copy of a held list. The other routes (a bookmarks file, notes, canvases, site styles) are explained in the import window's help, which reads nothing from another browser; passwords are out of scope (D52)

IM-14.note: progress per data type (a spinner, then a check), then a summary with counts per type and the skipped items with reasons; Done shows the imported folder in the sidebar (its Space, the pinned section open, the folder in view). Bookmarks are made out of sight, in parts, and their folder is shown whole, at once (D62): while 20,000 are added, the browser window’s longest freeze is under 0.1 s; 100,000 take about 34 s, with the window’s longest freeze about 0.34 s and main’s longest stall about 0.57 s (saving the state). A file the source browser holds (it can't be copied) shows "Chrome is using some of its files. Quit Chrome and try again, or import the rest" with Try again; the types it could read can still be imported. History shows the pages read, then added; Done says they're in History and the command bar; what History can't keep is listed with the reason. The summary lists every item left out with its reason: skipped bookmarks (also in a folder that holds nothing else), those past 200,000 bookmarks in one file, list or profile (folders don’t count, so the summary and the selection count agree), lines that aren’t links, and a profile’s file that couldn’t be read (“Work: history couldn’t be read (the file is damaged)”). Until the folder shows, nothing lists its tabs (D65): not the command bar (by title, by address or among recent tabs), the recent-tab switcher or the Library. One the user reached anyway and placed stays where they put it, and the folder leaves it out. A quit or a failure part-way takes back exactly the tabs the import made, by id, wherever they are, and nothing of the user’s; a crash part-way leaves none either, as the next start removes tabs that no section shows. Restore Data part-way stops the import first: its tabs are removed without going to the Archive, and the import window says “The import stopped: data was restored from a backup.” Copies of the other browser’s files go in a folder under Orbit’s user data, removed at quit (a copy still being made too) and cleared at startup (D58)

IM-07.note: Chromium's History, Firefox's places.sqlite and Safari's History.db (macOS-unverified), read from copies a window of rows at a time, into the chosen profile's history: each page with its title, visit and typed counts and its newest visits (up to 20). History (⌘Y / Ctrl+H) lists them and the command bar suggests and completes them at once; no tab is made and nothing loads. Left out: browsers' own pages, hidden pages, frame loads (Chromium subframes; Firefox embeds, framed links, downloads). History keeps the 50,000 most recent pages: a larger history keeps its newest and the summary counts the rest. 100,000 pages take about 2 s, with main's longest stall about 50–110 ms and none in the windows; the profile's history is written once, as a snapshot

IM-15.note: the same browser or file again makes a new "Imported from <Browser> (2)" folder (then (3)…), never merging into or changing the first. History de-duplicates silently: a page already imported gains only the visits it lacked, so its counts aren't doubled. Passwords aren't imported (D52)

IM-16.note: after onboarding's import of a history, the Done step offers the six sites visited most (each by its most-visited page, or its home page when that's a search): the first three as Favorites, the rest as pinned tabs. IM-17.note: Export Pinned Items as Bookmarks… in the File menu (macOS-unverified: Orbit has no menu bar elsewhere), the command bar, and Settings → General → Import and export (with Include Today tabs) writes a standard bookmarks HTML file through the system's save dialog: the Favorites a folder (one per profile when there are several), each Space a folder of its pinned section with its folders nested as they are, a split's tabs in its place; Today's tabs only when chosen, as a Today folder in their Space. IM-09.note: A Chromium-family profile's extensions are listed on the types step, from its Preferences and Secure Preferences (read from copies; a name kept only in the manifest is read from it, in its default language): pinned ones first, the browser's own left out.
